title: When the Guard Adds Nothing: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for LLM‑Produced Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=300 paired tasks) to measure whether a conservative generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) pipeline increases the probability that an LLM‑produced vendor CLI configuration passes a deterministic validator versus direct LLM generation. The design froze a single shared initial candidate per task (one generator call shared by both arms) and permitted at most one automatic repair call for the guarded arm if the shared initial failed. Under the declared generator snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558ed...) and the curated 300‑task multi‑vendor manifest, every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: baseline = 300/300; guarded = 300/300. The paired contingency table is n11=300, n10=n01=n00=0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p=1.00; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00,0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Because no initial failures occurred, the preregistered single‑repair policy was never invoked (repair_call_count=0). We release the full preregistration, task manifest, prompts, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts with canonical SHA‑256 hashes to enable exact reproduction and controlled follow‑ups.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to convert operator intent into vendor CLI fragments for NetOps. Operational adoption depends on reliability: generated changes must not violate syntactic constraints, resource assignments, or workflow safety invariants. A common defensive architecture is generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R): generation produces a candidate, a deterministic validator checks conservative safety rules, and an automatic repair attempts bounded corrections when validation fails. Yet quantified evidence about the marginal value of a bounded repair stage—holding generator, prompt, and validator fixed—is scarce.
Research question. Under a preregistered paired design in which the same initial generator candidate is shared between two conditions (baseline: validator(initial); guarded: validator(initial) or one automatic repair if initial fails), does permitting a single automatic repair call increase the per‑task probability of producing a validator‑passing configuration?
Contributions. (1) A machine‑readable preregistration frozen before execution (study_hosted_netops_gvr_v1_cnd_7a3f2b1e; preregistration SHA‑256 = a85d66d4c6ce2275e2d8c820f96c610532dbb5452bebb3fe108848f9dc38cdf6). (2) A curated 300‑task multi‑vendor manifest and a conservative deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) archived with canonical hashes (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a7...). (3) A confirmatory paired analysis executed exactly as preregistered (exact McNemar two‑sided test; paired bootstrap CI). (4) Full public archival of raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts with SHA‑256 checksums for exact replay (execution/execution_manifest.json lists all artifacts).
sections.related_work: Positioning. Recent work has explored LLM‑assisted intent translation and intent‑driven configuration generation (e.g., Nguyen et al., 2024; Chakraborty et al., 2024) and the use of verifier/validator layers for operational safety (Bagpipe / Weitz et al., 2016). Tool‑assisted self‑refinement and bounded self‑correction architectures (INTERACSPARQL and followups) motivated our bounded single‑repair policy. Unlike model‑leaderboard studies whose principal contribution is ranking, our experiment isolates an operational question: the incremental utility of a single bounded repair call for deterministic validator pass rates under a frozen generator snapshot and prompt. All cited prior works above are verified and used for design choices and conservative validator rules (see Cited Record Ids).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The full preregistration (study_hosted_netops_gvr_v1_cnd_7a3f2b1e; SHA‑256 above) fixed the paired design, analysis plan, stopping rules, random seeds, and allowed deviations. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the difference in per‑task probability that the guarded arm yields a validator‑pass versus the baseline, paired across tasks.
Task manifest and validator. We used a curated 300‑task multi‑vendor manifest limited to vendor CLI fragments (Cisco IOS, JunOS, Arista). Each manifest entry encodes initial state, intent, required safe sequence constraints (e.g., down‑before‑change, make‑before‑break), and expected final state. The manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a7...). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) implements conservative checks: CLI parsing/canonicalization; syntactic correctness; interface existence and assignment invariants; workflow invariants (must‑be‑down rules, minimum‑active constraints); and destructive‑pattern detection. Validator traces include parsed_command_count, required_command_count, touched fields, normalized final_configuration, and explicit pass/fail verdict; representative scoring artifacts are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; SHA‑256 = 1c3cbbeb30cb9d0...).
Generator, prompt, and repair policy. The declared generator snapshot is gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558ed...). Prompts and the repair prompt template were frozen and archived prior to model calls. The execution contract specified one shared initial generation per task (one model call shared between arms). The guarded arm was permitted at most one automatic repair LLM call if and only if the shared initial failed validation; repair budget=1 per task. Provider call traces and cached calls are archived (execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/).
Execution fidelity and reproducibility. The run used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 in scientific_confirmatory mode. All raw outputs, provider traces, scoring artifacts, and hashes are enumerated in execution/execution_manifest.json; representative paths and SHA‑256 values are referenced throughout the manuscript. The preregistered analysis code (paired_binary_analysis_v1) was executed without modification. Analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = a39fd3386c94...).
Statistical tests. The preregistered primary test is exact McNemar (two‑sided) on the paired 2×2 contingency table (n11,n10,n01,n00). A paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the paired difference used 10,000 resamples with seed=1729. Pre‑specified secondary analyses included per‑vendor paired tests with Bonferroni correction (family α=0.05→per‑comparison α≈0.0167).
sections.results:
Execution bookkeeping (artifact‑grounded). Planned episodes = 600 (300 tasks × 2 arms using a shared initial); completed episodes = 600; failed episodes = 0. Model calls used = 300 (one shared initial generation per task); repair calls permitted but not invoked (repair_call_count = 0). All raw outputs and provider traces are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json lists every artifact and hash). Representative artifacts: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a7...), execution/responses/*.txt and execution/scoring/*.json (examples cited below).
Confirmatory outcome (canonical values from archived analysis). Every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: baseline_success_count = 300/300; guarded_success_count = 300/300. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = a39fd3386c94...) is n11 = 300, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because there were no initial validator failures, the preregistered single‑repair policy was never exercised.
Per‑vendor preregistered secondary tests (preregistered handling). The preregistration required per‑vendor paired comparisons. The observed global discordance (n10+n01) = 0. Because discordance sums to zero across the full task set, every disjoint subgroup (including per‑vendor task subsets defined in the canonical task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 above) necessarily has zero discordant pairs as well. Consequently, each pre‑specified vendor subgroup yielded n11 = vendor_task_count and n10=n01=n00=0; the McNemar test is non‑informative in each subgroup under these observed counts. The manifest enumerates vendor membership for every task and is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a7...); auditors may replay or re‑slice the manifest to examine other regimes. Representative per‑episode scoring artifacts (validator traces) are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 1c3cbbeb30cb9d0..., execution/scoring/task-000002-baseline.json SHA‑256 = f64c4b757a27..., execution/scoring/task-000003-baseline.json SHA‑256 = b25c6d0f58d9...).
Representative diagnostics. Validator traces provide structured evidence: parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, and explicit violation lists. Example episode (artifact): execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 1c3cbbeb30cb9d0...) records parsed_command_count=4, required_command_count=4, valid=true, and the canonical final_configuration. Three representative episodes (task‑000001..000003) are included in the archived bundle; each shows identical shared initial / baseline / guarded outputs that passed the validator (artifact paths and hashes are archived).
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the frozen generator snapshot, prompt, and task manifest evaluated here, the generator produced validator‑compliant configurations for every sampled intent; a bounded single repair cannot increase validator pass probability when there are no initial failures. The statistical result (paired difference=0.00; p=1.00; CI=[0.00,0.00]) is therefore an accurate, artifact‑grounded reflection of the observed data.
Implications. Designers should not assume that adding an automatic repair stage will always increase conservative validator pass rates; utility depends on generator error rates for the deployment distribution. When generator accuracy is already high on a target manifest, the repair stage may add cost (latency, extra model calls, complexity) without deterministic pass‑rate benefit under the bounded policy we evaluated.
Why this ceiling arose and recommended follow‑ups. The archive permits controlled follow‑ups to probe regimes where repairs may help: (1) increase task difficulty or inject adversarial constraints into the manifest; (2) use independent (non‑shared) initial draws per arm so generator variability can create initial failures; (3) allow iterative repair (repair budget>1) or human‑in‑the‑loop repair; (4) evaluate other generator snapshots. All artifacts needed to reproduce the run and to replay alternative configurations are archived with canonical SHA‑256 hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json). We recommend a systematic series of follow‑ups that vary task difficulty, repair budget, and generator snapshot while retaining the same conservative validator to measure repair marginal benefit across regimes.
Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded). Internal validity: the shared‑initial design isolates repair marginality but reduces sensitivity to generator variance and can produce ceiling effects when generator accuracy is high. Execution determinism is supported by archived seeds and provider traces (execution/provider_calls/ and call_cache). Construct validity: our deterministic validator intentionally targets conservative, observable invariants (syntax, interface assignments, workflow constraints); it omits full dynamic emulation and some routing semantics—some operational hazards detectable only by richer emulation are not measured here. External validity: a single generator snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini), a single prompt family, and a curated 300‑task manifest limit generalization. Conclusion validity: zero observed discordant pairs makes significance testing non‑informative for demonstrating repair benefit; the null is nonetheless a valid empirical outcome. All these procedural facts and the underlying artifacts are archived and hash‑signed for auditors to inspect and to enable targeted replication with altered settings (paths and hashes cited above).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that compared a deterministic G‑V‑R pipeline (bounded to one repair attempt) against direct generation in a shared‑initial design. Under the frozen manifest, prompt, and generator snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini), every shared initial candidate passed the conservative deterministic validator and the preregistered single repair was never invoked. Observed paired difference = 0.00 (n11=300; exact McNemar p=1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI=[0.00,0.00]). The artifact bundle—preregistration, canonical task manifest, generator prompt templates, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts—are released with canonical SHA‑256 hashes to enable exact reproduction and controlled follow‑ups that alter task difficulty, generator snapshot, prompt design, or repair budget to probe regimes where automatic repair may yield benefit.

limitations: Single model snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluated — results do not generalize to other models or model versions.

Deterministic validator implements a conservative subset of operational hazards (syntactic checks, interface and workflow invariants) and omits dynamic/emulation‑level checks and deeper routing semantics.

Curated 300‑task manifest may not include adversarial or out‑of‑distribution failure modes; under the chosen prompt and model snapshot every shared initial candidate passed the validator (ceiling effect), limiting the ability to measure G‑V‑R improvements under the preregistered one‑repair policy.

Shared initial‑candidate design (preregistered) fixes the same initial generation for both arms to isolate repair effect; this reduces sensitivity to generator variability and can mask repair value when the generator is already accurate on the task set.
Only a single automatic repair attempt was permitted per task; iterative or human‑in‑the‑loop repair policies were not evaluated.
Automated contamination detection cannot eliminate memorization risk entirely; the preregistered contamination summary reported zero flagged pairs but residual uncertainty remains.
